episode_title: Avoiding Private Equity Pitfalls with Mark Gartner of RLH Equity Partners

real_qa.q: What five questions should a founder ask a private equity firm on an introductory call to evaluate if they are a good fit?
real_qa.r: The five questions are: (1) Do you have capital under your control, and when was your most recent fund raised and how much capital remains? (2) How many professional services transactions has your firm completed? (3) Why did you reach out to me specifically? (4) How do you add value beyond capital? (5) What is your philosophy around culture? A bonus sixth question addresses valuation methodology based on organic growth rates, margins, and revenue per client.
real_qa.requete: five questions to ask private equity firm initial call

real_qa.q: What organic growth rates do professional services companies typically achieve when benefiting from technology trends?
real_qa.r: RLH Equity Partners has been successful with companies that benefit from technology change or technology complexity, and it is common to see organic growth in the companies they invest in at 15 to 20 percent or more as these macro trends rise.
real_qa.requete: professional services organic growth rate technology trends

real_qa.q: How does RLH Equity Partners structure founder retention after acquiring a professional services company?
real_qa.r: RLH partners with founders who are enthusiastic about retaining upwards of 40 percent of the equity alongside the firm and continuing to run the business, ensuring leadership and cultural continuity. Before closing, they develop a 90 to 120-day plan with no surprises and philosophical alignment to protect the culture that made the business attractive to invest in.
real_qa.requete: founder equity retention professional services private equity

real_qa.q: What red flags indicate a private equity outreach email is spam or mass-market spray-and-pray?
real_qa.r: If the email contains an unsubscribe button at the bottom, it is part of a spray-and-pray campaign and should be ignored. Also ignore emails that do not use your name or company name, those using long-form legalistic versions like 'comma LLC,' or text that appears cut and pasted. You can tell when text has been cut and pasted into an email by natural human detectors.
real_qa.requete: how to spot spam private equity outreach email

real_qa.q: What are the key KPIs that RLH Equity Partners evaluates when assessing a professional services company valuation?
real_qa.r: For companies with revenue north of $20 million, RLH first looks at organic growth of 15 to 20 percent or more and the margins being generated, which implies revenue quality. They also examine how much revenue each client generates—whether half a million to a million dollars or more per client—and whether that revenue is increasing year over year, plus additional KPIs captured in their Professional Services Evaluation Scorecard.
real_qa.requete: professional services company valuation KPIs metrics

real_qa.q: Why should a founder not fear talking to private equity investors even if not ready to sell?
real_qa.r: Talking with investors is not that risky because you do not have to tell them anything you do not want to, and you are only signing up for a 30 or 45 minute conversation. Getting to know a couple of investors allows you to listen to the questions they are asking and understand how they think, which can inform your strategy and provide value even if those investors do not end up investing in your business.
real_qa.requete: should business owner talk to private equity investors before ready

guest.bio_context: Mark Gartner is a Managing Director at RLH Equity Partners, a firm that has been operating for 42 years and has focused exclusively on professional services investments for the past couple of decades. He specializes in helping high-growth services-based companies scale from $20-30 million in revenue to $100 million and beyond through organic growth strategies that prioritize culture, founder partnerships, and minimal debt usage.
